subject: social
title: Leaders and Voting
about: Leaders as roles, from the teacher and principal up to the mayor, governor and president, who makes laws, and how people choose leaders by voting. NC 1.C&G.1.1 and 1.C&G.1.2.
tip: Say a place (school, town, state, country) and let him name the leader; never use a current leader's name.

cards.q: What do we call a person who guides a group and helps make choices?
cards.note: A leader helps the group decide what to do.

cards.q: Who is the leader of your class?
cards.note: The teacher leads the class and helps everyone learn.
The principal is in charge of every class in the school.

cards.q: Who leads a town or city?
cards.note: The mayor works at town hall or city hall.

cards.q: Who leads our state, North Carolina?
cards.note: The governor works in Raleigh, the capital of North Carolina.

cards.q: Who leads our whole country, the United States?
cards.note: There is one president for the whole country.

cards.q: Where does the president live and work?
cards.note: The White House is in Washington, D.C., the capital of our country.

cards.q: Who makes the laws for the whole country?
cards.note: Congress is a big group of people chosen by voters.

cards.q: Who makes the laws for North Carolina?
cards.note: The General Assembly meets in Raleigh, our state capital.

cards.q: Who is in charge in a court of law?
cards.note: A judge listens to both sides and makes sure the court is fair.

cards.q: How do people choose their leaders?
What do we call it when people vote to pick a leader?
cards.note: On election day, voters go to a voting place to vote.

cards.q: What do we call the paper or screen where you mark your vote?
cards.note: You mark your choice on the ballot, and your vote is kept private.

cards.q: Who can vote for the president in our country?
cards.note: Citizens who are 18 or older can vote.

cards.q: How can a class fairly pick which game to play?
cards.note: Voting is a fair way for a group to make a choice.
